strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Allows Runtime-created task, run, journey, checkpoint, and ledger state to be version-gated before autonomous controllers depend on durable replay.
Keeps durable compatibility decisions inside Runtime/Store instead of letting CLI, prose, or file shape accidentally authorize reads or writes.
Prevents tool/recovery ledger mutation when the local durable store advertises a malformed, unknown, or future schema.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development, runtime_permission_enforcement, and controlled_workspace_tools by adding a Runtime-owned durable store schema manifest and fail-closed compatibility gate.
answers.new_capability: Runtime/store first-touch creates or adopts a bounded .brownie/store-schema.json manifest for current v1 layout, and store-backed Runtime methods plus durable task/run/journey/checkpoint/ledger operations reject malformed or future manifests before mutation.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Existing payload-level schema_version fields documented individual protocol/checkpoint shapes but did not provide a release-level store schema gate that could distinguish current v1, legacy missing-manifest state, corrupt manifests, or future incompatible layouts.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A headless controller could continue reading or writing local durable state whose store-level layout was unknown to the current Runtime, weakening replay, recovery, and migration safety.
answers.non_duplicative: This closes the durable-schema-version-and-migration blocker; it is not another MCP approval/recovery phase, CI workflow phase, protocol/event canonization phase, or module decomposition phase.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The behavior is enforced inside brownie-store and BrownieStore::from_env_or_cwd without adding JSON-RPC methods or client projection APIs.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The only new durable artifact is the local schema manifest required for compatibility; docs and audit manifests are updated as existing release-readiness evidence.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Store-backed Runtime methods now ensure the durable schema before durable work; task/run/journey/checkpoint/ledger reads and writes create/adopt the v1 manifest on missing current-layout stores and fail closed for malformed, wrong-id, non-current, or future-version manifests. Store-free status and diagnostics remain store-free.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: External controllers can rely on Runtime refusing incompatible durable replay state before producing new task, recovery, approval, journey, checkpoint, or ledger evidence.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the P0 durable-schema-version-and-migration blocker while keeping Runtime Release Ready false until CI release gate, protocol/event canonization, module decomposition reevaluation, platform/deadline/durability hardening, and owner license/publish decisions are resolved.

implementation_audit_classification.evidence: brownie-store defines .brownie/store-schema.json with schema id, manifest format version, store schema version, minimum runtime schema version, current state, and bounded migration source; the manifest contains no raw prompt, provider response, file content, absolute/canonical path, secret, environment, executable content, or process output values.

TaskStore::ensure_durable_schema creates a v1 manifest for new stores, adopts missing-manifest v1 layout under an exclusive migration lock, validates strict known fields, and fails closed for corrupt, wrong-id, non-current, or unsupported future manifests.

implementation_audit_classification.surface: Store-backed Runtime and durable mutation coverage
implementation_audit_classification.evidence: BrownieStore::from_env_or_cwd ensures schema compatibility before store-backed Runtime methods proceed; task state, ledger, headless continuation, run session, journey, objective admission, completion finalization, active ModePack, and ModePack candidate read/write paths check schema before mutation through their read or write entrypoints. Store-free status remains outside the durable gate.
The phase does not set runtime_release_ready=true, change license/publish metadata, or start non-durable-schema phases; remaining P0/P1 blockers stay open.

future store schema version is treated as compatible by default

compatibility decision is delegated to CLI, VSIX, prose, model output, MCP metadata, or external controller state

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: RRP-4 changes the current phase manifest and Runtime release-readiness audit while closing durable-schema-version-and-migration. Review must confirm durable schema metadata is bounded, store-backed Runtime methods and store mutations fail closed for incompatible manifests, legacy missing-manifest v1 layout is adopted under a lock, and Runtime Release Ready remains false.

exit_criteria: Store-level durable schema manifest is created for new .brownie stores with bounded metadata only.
Existing missing-manifest v1-shaped .brownie layouts are adopted under an exclusive migration lock.
Malformed, wrong-id, non-current, or future durable schema manifests fail closed before task/run/journey/checkpoint/ledger mutation.
Store-backed Runtime methods through BrownieStore::from_env_or_cwd ensure durable schema compatibility before durable JSON-RPC work proceeds.
Tests cover manifest initialization, legacy adoption, malformed rejection, future-version rejection before mutation, and minimum-runtime-version rejection.

Incompatible durable schema manifests stop Runtime/store durable mutation before new evidence is written.

safety_boundary: Rust Runtime and brownie-store remain durable schema, replay, admission, ledger, checkpoint, and mutation authority.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection layers and do not decide store compatibility.
Schema manifests are bounded compatibility metadata, not authority from prompts, provider output, file content, paths, secrets, executable content, or process output.
non_goals: Does not claim Runtime Release Ready.
Does not change license, publish settings, tags, release assets, or public OSS release posture.
Does not start CI hardening, protocol/event canonization, module decomposition, platform/deadline/durability hardening, or hosted scheduler/daemon/adapter work.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected relying only on per-payload schema_version fields because they do not gate the store layout as a whole.
Rejected best-effort reads of corrupt or future manifests because release durability requires fail-closed behavior.
Rejected ledgering raw paths or content as migration evidence because the release boundary forbids sensitive/raw value ledgering.
technical_debt: runtime-release-guard-ci, protocol-event-canonization, runtime-module-decomposition-reevaluation, and platform-deadline-durability-hardening remain open Runtime blockers.
Owner license/publish decisions remain required before OSS Release Ready.
next_capability_rationale: Continue with a later explicit Runtime-owned blocker phase rather than claiming Runtime Release Ready.

runtime_release_dod: RRP-4 closes the local Runtime durable schema manifest and migration/fail-closed gate for v1 .brownie state.
Runtime Release Ready remains false until remaining Runtime P0/P1 blockers and owner license/publish decisions are resolved.
runtime_boundary_contracts: No new RPC surface is added; Store-backed Runtime methods and existing durable operations enforce compatibility internally.
CLI and VSIX remain thin clients over Runtime-owned contracts.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: External scheduling, queueing, worker leases, hosted isolation, retry policy, metrics, alerts, SLA, tenant administration, billing, and secret-provider operations remain outside this local Runtime v0 phase.
external_adapter_responsibilities: Forge, pull request, review, notification, SIEM, OTel, language verifier, customer integration, and hosted MCP adapter responsibilities remain outside RRP-4.
commercial_solution_readiness: Packaging, distribution, signing, notarization, enterprise administration, operational runbooks, support, and commercial release decisions remain out of scope.
Cargo license and publish settings remain owner-decision items and are not changed by RRP-4.
